sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Kim Severson, and this is The Daily.

sentences.en: A gloves-off trade war with America is uniting Canadians from all corners of the country against its southern neighbor.
sentences.zh: 一场撕破脸的对美贸易战正将来自全国各个角落的加拿大人团结起来，共同对抗其南部邻国。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Matina Steves-Gridneff, on what that trade war means for the future of the relationship
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事马蒂娜·斯蒂夫斯-格里德内夫将讲述这场贸易战对两国关系未来的意义
zh_words: 马蒂娜·斯蒂夫斯-格里德内夫

sentences.en: and how this fight is shifting the country's politics, its culture, and its place on the global stage.
sentences.zh: 以及这场争端如何改变该国的政治、文化及其在全球舞台上的地位。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, March 13th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月13日，星期四。

sentences.en: Matina, you've been traveling across Canada reporting on what's turned out to be a very big news week.
sentences.zh: 马蒂娜，你一直在加拿大各地采访，报道了一周以来的重大新闻。

sentences.en: Thank you for taking the time to come on the show.
sentences.zh: 感谢你抽空来到节目中。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me, Kim.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我，金。

sentences.en: So, coming into his presidency, I think there was an expectation that Trump might make waves on matters of international diplomacy.
sentences.zh: 所以，在他上任之初，人们似乎普遍预计特朗普会在国际外交事务上掀起波澜。

sentences.en: But I don't think many of us had made Canadians really, really angry on their bingo card.
sentences.zh: 但我想我们很多人都没料到会把加拿大人惹得如此暴怒。

sentences.en: Oh, totally.
sentences.zh: 哦，完全是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, I took up my posting as Canada Bureau Chief in AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我在8月份上任了加拿大分社长。

sentences.en: And I thought this was going to be a good posting for my work-life balance.
sentences.zh: 我原本以为这份工作对我的工作与生活平衡会很有利。

sentences.en: Little did I know.
sentences.zh: 我当时可真没想到。

sentences.en: I mean, it's been a really extraordinary stretch since the election, for sure.
sentences.zh: 我是说，自大选以来，这段时期确实非常不寻常。

sentences.en: So, let's rewind a little and just remind me of how we got here.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们倒回一点，提醒我一下我们是怎么走到这一步的。

sentences.en: You know, we're in a place where Canadians who, you know, to many Americans seem very, very nice, have turned downright hostile and find themselves in such a political vice.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们现在的处境是，那些在许多美国人看来非常非常友善的加拿大人，已经变得极其敌对，并陷入了如此严重的政治夹缝中。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: I mean, I think the first signs that something was going to go wrong emerged in early December,
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为最早出现问题迹象是在12月初，

sentences.en: when Prime Minister Justin Trudeau flew to Mar-a-Lago to sit down for dinner with President-elect at the time, Trump.
sentences.zh: 当时总理贾斯廷·特鲁多飞往海湖庄园，与时任当选总统特朗普共进晚餐。

sentences.en: And the dinner, you know, was feeded as a success for Trudeau to be able to get FaceTime with Trump.
sentences.zh: 那次晚宴，你知道的，被宣传为特鲁多取得成功的一次机会，得以与特朗普面对面交流。

sentences.en: And it seemed cordial enough.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来也算融洽。

sentences.en: There were, like, photos of everyone smiling and jokes.
sentences.zh: 有那种每个人都在微笑的照片和笑话。

sentences.en: And tonight we're getting some new details about that Trump-Trudeau dinner from two people who were at the table.
sentences.zh: 今晚我们从两位在场的知情人士那里获得了关于那次特朗普与特鲁多晚宴的新细节。

sentences.en: But it does sound like that's when Trump sort of started raising complaints about the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但听起来确实是从那个时候开始，特朗普开始对美国与加拿大的关系提出抱怨。

sentences.en: relationship with Canada.
sentences.zh: 与加拿大的关系。

sentences.en: Fox News is reporting that Trudeau warned Trump that his tariff proposal would kill the Canadian economy,
sentences.zh: 福克斯新闻报道称，特鲁多曾警告特朗普，他的关税提案将摧毁加拿大经济，

sentences.en: to which Trump replied that Canada could then become the 51st state and that Trudeau could be governor.
sentences.zh: 对此特朗普回答说，那加拿大可以成为第51个州，而特鲁多可以当州长。

sentences.en: And made the supposed joke of Canada becoming the 51st state of the United States.
sentences.zh: 并开玩笑了般地提出了加拿大成为美国第51个州的说法。

sentences.en: That meaning did not appear to go well.
sentences.zh: 这个含义似乎并没有被很好地接受。

sentences.en: Well, the Canadian delegation brushed that off at the time, but it would come back to haunt them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，加拿大代表团当时把这当作玩笑随手打发了，但这件事后来成了他们的挥之不去的阴影。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think a lot of us did.
sentences.zh: 我想我们很多人都这么想。

sentences.en: And no one knew if it was one of the many things that he says that you don't know whether to take seriously or not.
sentences.zh: 而且没有人知道这是否只是他的众多言论之一——你根本不知道该不该把它们当真。

sentences.en: For sure.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I think that at first that was generally seen as like a troll.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为起初这普遍被看作是一种网络钓鱼式的挑衅。

sentences.en: A lot of people thought it was quite personal to Trudeau because we knew Trump doesn't like Trudeau much from his first presidency.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为这针对特鲁多个人色彩很浓，因为我们知道特朗普从第一任期起就不太喜欢特鲁多。

sentences.en: But I think that we started realizing it is probably something more ominous when Trump gave a press conference on January 7th.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，随着特朗普在1月7日举行记者会，我们开始意识到这可能更加不妙。

sentences.en: So thank you all for coming.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家的光临。

sentences.en: We'll take a couple of questions.
sentences.zh: 我们回答几个问题。

sentences.en: And our own colleague David Sanger of The New York Times asked him about his claims on Greenland, which is an autonomous area of Denmark and the Panama Canal and Canada.
sentences.zh: 我们的同事、《纽约时报》的大卫·萨恩格向他询问了他对格陵兰岛（丹麦的自治领地）、巴拿马运河以及加拿大的主张。

sentences.en: Can you assure the world that as you try to get control of these areas, you are not going to use military or economic coercion?
sentences.zh: 你能向世界保证，在试图控制这些地区时，你不会使用军事或经济胁迫吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: And he specifically asked, are you going to use force to annex these places?
sentences.zh: 他具体追问，你们会使用武力吞并这些地方吗？

sentences.en: And Trump said...
sentences.zh: 特朗普说……

sentences.en: Economic force.
sentences.zh: 经济武力。

sentences.en: Economic force.
sentences.zh: 经济武力。

sentences.en: Because Canada and the United States, that would really be something.
sentences.zh: 因为加拿大和美国，那可真有点意思了。

sentences.en: So by late January, it becomes clear President Trump is being serious about imposing tariffs on all Canadian and Mexican goods being imported into the United States.
sentences.zh: 因此，到了1月底，特朗普总统对所有进口到美国的加拿大和墨西哥商品征收关税动真格的，这变得显而易见。

sentences.en: I mean, you have to remember, Canada and the United States are each other's closest trading partners.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你必须记住，加拿大和美国是彼此最亲密的贸易伙伴。

sentences.en: The United States is the destination for about 80 percent of goods that Canada exports, including, for example, its oil and gas.
sentences.zh: 美国是加拿大出口商品的大约80%的目的地，其中包括例如它的石油和天然气。

sentences.en: And so this is a core existential economic relationship.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一项核心的生死攸关的经济关系。

sentences.en: And those tariffs that President Trump is threatening to slap on Canadian goods, they have the potential to derail the Canadian economy.
sentences.zh: 而特朗普总统威胁要对加拿大商品加征的那些关税，有可能彻底破坏加拿大经济。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And we've talked on the show before about the threat of tariffs and the way Trump justified them at the outset,
sentences.zh: 我们以前在节目中谈论过关税的威胁，以及特朗普最初为之辩护的方式，

sentences.en: is that he would be using them as a way of forcing our neighboring countries to reduce both migrant traffic and drug traffic from coming into the U.S.
sentences.zh: 就是他将以此作为迫使我们的邻国减少流入美国的移民和毒品走流量的手段。

sentences.en: But these are not, seems to me, major problems at the border of Canada.
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，这些并不是加拿大边境上的主要问题。

sentences.en: So was there a sense among the Canadian government that this was about something else?
sentences.zh: 那么加拿大政府是否有一种感觉，觉得这其实是关于其他事情？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And I think where we really came to see this and it took some time for the reporting to come together is over the course of two phone calls that President Trump and Prime Minister Trudeau held on February 3rd.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们真正看清这一点——尽管报道整合花了一些时间——是通过特朗普总统与特鲁多总理在2月3日进行的两通电话。

sentences.en: So what happens on those calls is that President Trump lays down for Prime Minister Trudeau a number of grievances that he has with the economic and trade relationship between the two countries.
sentences.zh: 这两通电话发生的情况是，特朗普总统向特鲁多总理列举了他对两国经济和贸易关系的一系列不满。

sentences.en: These were generally well-known problems or concerns on the American side.
sentences.zh: 这些对美方来说通常是众所周知的问题或担忧。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国希望更好地进入加拿大的乳制品市场和银行部门。

sentences.en: wanted better access to the Canadian dairy market and the banking sector.
sentences.zh: 但是随后特朗普总统提出了更根本的问题。

sentences.en: But then President Trump raised something much more fundamental.
sentences.zh: 他告诉特鲁多，据我们的消息来源称，他显然是在照着一份备忘录念。

sentences.en: He tells Trudeau, and apparently he's reading off a memo, according to our sources.
sentences.zh: 他告诉特鲁多，我不喜欢我们两国之间的边界条约。

sentences.en: He tells Trudeau, and I don't like the border treaty between our two countries.
sentences.zh: 这是一项划定两国分界线的1908年条约。

sentences.en: This is a 1908 treaty that demarcates the boundary between the two nations.
sentences.zh: 而特朗普总统直接告诉特鲁多总理，他认为该条约无效，应当重新审视。

sentences.en: And President Trump just tells Prime Minister Trudeau he thinks it's not valid and should be revisited.
sentences.zh: 他还告诉特鲁多，他不喜欢两国共享水资源的方式。

sentences.en: He also tells him he doesn't like the way the two countries share water.
sentences.zh: 我们知道特朗普总统对加拿大的水资源非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: We know President Trump is really interested in Canada's water.
sentences.zh: 他认为加拿大的水资源太多了。

sentences.en: He thinks Canada has too much of it.
sentences.zh: 他还向特鲁多提出，他希望重新审视两国之间的水资源协议。

sentences.en: And he also raises to Trudeau that he wants to revisit water agreements between the two countries.
sentences.zh: 于是我们突然从“我不喜欢我们的贸易方式以及我们的经济是如何一体化的”，变成了“你这地方风景挺好啊”。

sentences.en: And so suddenly we go from, I don't like the way we trade and how our economies are integrated, to nice country you got there.
sentences.zh: 要是出了点什么事可就太可惜了。

sentences.en: Shame if something happened to it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这看起来真是一个非同寻常的时刻。

sentences.en: I mean, this seems like an extraordinary moment.
sentences.zh: 特朗普在电话里对特鲁多基本上说的是，我不尊重你们的边界或主权。

sentences.en: Here is Trump on the phone with Trudeau essentially saying, I don't respect your borders or your sovereignty.
sentences.zh: 加拿大政府此时对此作何反应？

sentences.en: How is the Canadian government reacting to all this at this point?
sentences.zh: 那通电话之后是一片震惊、愤怒和如临大敌的状态。

sentences.en: It was shock and anger and panic stations after that phone call.
sentences.zh: 特鲁多非常明确地表示，如果这一威胁付诸实施并成为现实，我们将用我们自己的关税对美国产品进行回击。

sentences.en: And Trudeau makes it quite clear that we're going to hit back on U.S.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个提醒人们的好时机，特鲁多正经历他任内的最后几周。

sentences.en: products with our own tariffs if this threat materializes and becomes reality.
sentences.zh: 他已经表示将辞职，我们预计他将在3月底离职。

sentences.en: And I think this is a good point to remind people, Trudeau is going through his last weeks in office.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管他已经快要卸任，他还是采取了这种相当强硬的姿态。

sentences.en: He has said he's going to resign and we're expecting him to be out of government by the end of March.
sentences.zh: 现在，当加拿大人面临来自邻国的生死挑战和经济危机时，加拿大人正在展现出我们的真正骨气。

sentences.en: And so he takes this quite aggressive stance, even though he's almost out of government.
sentences.zh: 这是他开始发表长篇大论并全力倚重的主题。

sentences.en: And now, as Canadians face from our neighbor an existential challenge, an economic crisis, Canadians are showing exactly what we are made of.
sentences.zh: 自由不是天经地义的。

sentences.en: And this is something he starts giving speeches on and leans into.
sentences.zh: 甚至连加拿大，也不是天经地义的。

sentences.en: Freedom is not a given.
sentences.zh: 这一切都不会凭空发生。

sentences.en: Even, even Canada, is not a given.
sentences.zh: 没有付出努力，这一切都无法延续。

sentences.en: None of those happen by accident.
sentences.zh: 他带着相当情绪化的语气说，我们没有挑起这场争端，但我们会为我们的国家挺身而出。

sentences.en: None of them will continue without effort.
sentences.zh: 我们是一个在能够外交时保持外交，但在必须战斗时绝不退缩的国家，蓄势待发。

sentences.en: Sort of quite emotionally, he says, we didn't ask for this fight, but we will stand up for our country.
sentences.zh: 而这起作用了。

sentences.en: We're a country that will be diplomatic when we can, but fight when we must, elbows up.
sentences.zh: 这些演讲确实激发了加拿大人的斗志。

sentences.en: And it works.
sentences.zh: 蓄势待发，朋友们。

sentences.en: These speeches do galvanize Canadians.
sentences.zh: 是时候蓄势待发了。

sentences.en: Elbows up, folks.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们准备好战斗了。

sentences.en: Elbows up time.
sentences.zh: 他们说“蓄势待发”（elbows up），借用了冰球运动的一个术语，表明他们想要保卫自己的国家。

sentences.en: It means we're about to fight.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，加拿大绝不会屈服。

sentences.en: They say elbows up, borrowing a term from hockey and showing that they want to defend their country.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不会向黑帮头子的戒指低头亲吻。

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, Canada will never bend.
sentences.zh: 公众的反应非常自然。

sentences.en: We will never kiss the gangster's ring.
sentences.zh: 战争已经正式打响，所以如果你是加拿大人，现在比以往任何时候都更重要的是去购买加拿大本土产品。

sentences.en: The public is really reacting very organically.
sentences.zh: 我们看到，标有“加拿大制造”的标志随处可见，杂货商正竖起国旗，告诉消费者哪些产品是加拿大制造的，以便他们能够优先选择这些产品而不是美国产品。

sentences.en: War is officially on, so if you're Canadian, now more than ever, it's so important to be shopping Canadian products.
sentences.zh: 喝一杯咖啡，它不是福爵（Folgers）。

sentences.en: We're seeing, by Canadian signs, grocers are putting up flags to tell consumers which products are made in Canada so that they can prefer them over American products.
sentences.zh: 我跟福爵咖啡一刀两断了。

sentences.en: Having a coffee, it is not Folgers.
sentences.zh: 现在喝的是加拿大咖啡。

sentences.en: I'm done with Folgers.
sentences.zh: 我是说，看着这种愤怒变成一种有形的东西，看着反美情绪不断酝酿，真是令人瞩目。

sentences.en: It is now Canadian coffee.
sentences.zh: 我们开始听到一些——可以说是真正非同寻常的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, it was remarkable to watch this anger become a visible thing, seeing anti-Americanist feelings foment.
sentences.zh: 加拿大人在冰球比赛中对美国国歌发出嘘声。

sentences.en: And we start hearing something, I mean, truly remarkable.
sentences.zh: 说到冰球，大家甚至对格雷茨基也感到愤怒，他在这里就像是个民族英雄。

sentences.en: Canadians booing the American national anthem in hockey games.
sentences.zh: 加拿大将永远不会屈服。

sentences.en: And while we're on the topic of hockey, folks are even angry with Gretzky, who's like a national hero here.
sentences.zh: 我们永远不会向黑帮头子的戒指低头亲吻。

sentences.en: He's like a symbol.
sentences.zh: 他就像是个象征。

sentences.en: Wayne Gretzky, the big Canadian hockey hero, right?
sentences.zh: 韦恩·格雷茨基，那个伟大的加拿大冰球英雄，对吧？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, also a close friend of Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他也是唐纳德·特朗普的密友。

sentences.en: And so he suddenly has this fall from grace and Canadians are treating him like a traitor.
sentences.zh: 因此他突然失宠了，加拿大人把他当成了叛徒。

sentences.en: So these feelings are just really brewing, are very powerful.
sentences.zh: 所以这种情绪正在酝酿，并且非常强烈。

sentences.en: They're finding expression in various ways across Canadian society.
sentences.zh: 它们正以各种方式在加拿大社会中表现出来。

sentences.en: This is not like a minority situation.
sentences.zh: 这绝不是少数人的情况。

sentences.en: I don't really want to play Canada's therapist here, but what's behind the reaction?
sentences.zh: 我并不是真的想扮演加拿大的心理医生，但这背后的反应是什么？

sentences.en: Is it defiance?
sentences.zh: 是挑衅吗？

sentences.en: Is it betrayal?
sentences.zh: 是背叛吗？

sentences.en: I mean, what do you think is unifying the Canadians at this point?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你认为现在是什么在凝聚着加拿大人？

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's all of the above.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为以上所有因素都有。

sentences.en: It's anger.
sentences.zh: 是愤怒。

sentences.en: It's betrayal.
sentences.zh: 是背叛。

sentences.en: Betrayal by a friend hurts so much more.
sentences.zh: 来自朋友的背叛伤害更深。

sentences.en: And from the political elite of the country, all the way down to the street and ordinary Canadians, the nation is going through a range of emotions.
sentences.zh: 从国家的政治精英到街头普通民众，整个国家正在经历各种各样的情绪。

sentences.en: Anger, fear, insecurity.
sentences.zh: 愤怒、恐惧、不安。

sentences.en: And I think it goes beyond being just a moment.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这已经不仅仅是一个阶段的事了。

sentences.en: It has the potential to alter the course of Canadian history.
sentences.zh: 它有可能改变加拿大历史的走向。

sentences.en: And we're already seeing the first sign of that.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到了最初的迹象。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温纳露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《连线》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基，我每天创作《拼写蜜蜂》和《信箱》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做色彩联觉的现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像刚才你们听到声音的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com slash games，今天就开始游戏吧。

sentences.en: Matina, you were telling us that what's happening in Canada in response to the trade wars and to the intense rhetoric coming from the Trump administration
sentences.zh: 玛蒂娜，你刚才告诉我们，加拿大针对贸易战以及来自特朗普政府的激烈言论所做出的反应

sentences.en: was beginning to change Canada in some extremely significant ways that really have long-term implications.
sentences.zh: 正开始以一些极其显著的方式改变加拿大，这确实有着深远的影响。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我你这是什么意思吗？

sentences.en: Well, Kim, back in January, when this problem was gathering pace, Justin Trudeau was resigning.
sentences.zh: 嗯，金，早在1月份，当这个问题日益严重时，贾斯廷·特鲁多就要辞职了。

sentences.en: His party, the Liberal Party, who have been in power for nearly 10 years, were facing dismal polls.
sentences.zh: 他的政党自由党已经执政近10年，正面临着惨淡的民调。

sentences.en: They were 20-plus percentage points behind the opposition, the Conservatives, led by Pierre Polievre.
sentences.zh: 他们的支持率比由皮埃尔·波利耶夫领导的反对党保守党落后20多个百分点。

sentences.en: And in the federal elections looming, it was sort of a foregone conclusion that the Conservatives were going to win.
sentences.zh: 在即将到来的联邦大选中，保守党获胜几乎是板上钉钉的事。

sentences.en: Polievre was going to be the new prime minister.
sentences.zh: 波利耶夫将成为新任总理。

sentences.en: He had these ideological and stylistic affiliations to the MAGA movement and the sort of more right-wing populist movement.
sentences.zh: 他在意识形态和风格上与MAGA运动以及那种更偏右翼的民粹主义运动有着联系。

sentences.en: And that was kind of what was going to happen in Canadian politics.
sentences.zh: 这就是加拿大政坛当时的发展方向。

sentences.en: But things started to rapidly change just as Trump escalated his menacing rhetoric about Canadian sovereignty and went ahead with his tariff threats.
sentences.zh: 但就在特朗普升级关于加拿大主权的威胁性言论并推进其关税威胁时，情况开始迅速发生变化。

sentences.en: Something, I mean, truly remarkable happens.
sentences.zh: 发生了一件可以说是真正非同寻常的事情。

sentences.en: And I spoke to pollsters.
sentences.zh: 我和民意调查专家交谈过。

sentences.en: One of them, a really seasoned pollster, told me that he's never seen this in his entire career.
sentences.zh: 其中一位经验丰富的民调专家告诉我，他在整个职业生涯中从未见过这种情况。

sentences.en: We go from, you know, the Liberal Party's dead and they're going to be going into political exile for a long, long time to this liberal revival.
sentences.zh: 我们从“你知道的，自由党已经完了，他们将长期流放于政坛之外”转变成了这场自由主义的复兴。

sentences.en: The anti-U.S., anti-Trump sentiment is basically doing huge favors to the Liberal Party, even rehabilitating the image of Justin Trudeau to a certain extent,
sentences.zh: 反美、反特朗普的情绪实际上对自由党产生了巨大的帮助，甚至在某种程度上修复了贾斯廷·特鲁多的形象，

sentences.en: who was loathed to the extent that he had to resign in early January, right?
sentences.zh: 他曾遭人痛恨到不得不于1月初辞职，对吧？

sentences.en: And so it sets the scene for a stunning and pretty rapid reversal of fortunes for the Liberal Party as it goes into a leadership race to elect its new leader,
sentences.zh: 因此，随着自由党进入选举新党魁的领导层竞选，这为该党财富惊人且相当迅速的逆转拉开了序幕，

sentences.en: the person who's going to replace Justin Trudeau as party chief and as prime minister.
sentences.zh: 也就是将取代贾斯廷·特鲁多担任党魁和总理的人。

sentences.en: So what happens?
sentences.zh: 那么发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, the party rallies in a dramatic way around one candidate.
sentences.zh: 嗯，该党以戏剧性的方式团结在了一位候选人周围。

sentences.en: His name is Mark Carney.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫马克·卡尼。

sentences.en: Mark Carney is not a politician.
sentences.zh: 马克·卡尼不是政客。

sentences.en: He's a political novice who hasn't held elected office, but has been in the public eye for many, many years, really his entire career.
sentences.zh: 他是一个没有担任过民选职务的政治新手，但在公众视野中已经很多很多年了，可以说贯穿了他的整个职业生涯。

sentences.en: He was the governor of the Bank of Canada during the global financial crisis of 2008.
sentences.zh: 他在2008年全球金融危机期间担任加拿大银行行长。

sentences.en: And then he went on to become the governor of the Bank of England during Brexit.
sentences.zh: 后来在英国脱欧期间，他担任了英格兰银行行长。

sentences.en: So Canadians know him as a solid economics policy guy.
sentences.zh: 因此，加拿大人认为他是一个稳健的经济政策专家。

sentences.en: For sure.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But people point out that Carney is not a natural-born politician.
sentences.zh: 但人们指出，卡尼并不是天生的政客。

sentences.en: He's not oozing charisma.
sentences.zh: 他身上没有那种个人魅力。

sentences.en: I think when he started his campaign in January, polling showed one in three Canadians only could recognize his photo, could name who he was.
sentences.zh: 我想他在1月份开始竞选时，民调显示只有三分之一的加拿大人能认出他的照片，能叫出他的名字。

sentences.en: And nonetheless, the moment he's in and the anti-Trump sentiment, the fear and concern Canadians are feeling and the anger just turbocharges his campaign.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他一参选，反特朗普情绪、加拿大人感受到的恐惧和担忧以及愤怒，就极大地推动了他的竞选。

sentences.en: So people are looking to Carney as someone who can, you know, potentially make a deal with Trump, but also steer the country through what will be a challenging economic period.
sentences.zh: 所以人们把卡尼视为一个既有可能与特朗普达成协议，又能引领国家度过充满挑战的经济时期的人。

sentences.en: You know, people think he knows what he's doing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，人们认为他知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: But Carney has a huge challenge in his hands, and that's that he has to be campaigning for his job as prime minister while being prime minister.
sentences.zh: 但卡尼手头面临着一个巨大的挑战，那就是他必须在担任总理的同时，还要为自己的总理职位展开竞选。

sentences.en: He's expected to get sworn in any day now.
sentences.zh: 预计他随时都可能宣誓就职。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Can you remind me how this works?
sentences.zh: 你能提醒我这是怎么运作的吗？

sentences.en: So he's serving as prime minister, and then he has to run fairly soon again as prime minister.
sentences.zh: 所以他担任总理，然后很快又必须以总理身份再次参选？

sentences.en: Can you just give me the little Canadian Parliament 101?
sentences.zh: 你能给我简单介绍一下加拿大议会的基础知识吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: It is a little complicated.
sentences.zh: 这有点复杂。

sentences.en: But Canada has a sort of parliamentary system where the leader of the party in power is the prime minister.
sentences.zh: 但加拿大实行的是一种议会制，执政党领袖就是总理。

sentences.en: And so Mr. Carney has been elected as leader of the Liberal Party, and so he will be sworn in as prime minister.
sentences.zh: 因此卡尼先生已被选为自由党领袖，所以他将宣誓就职成为总理。

sentences.en: But by Canadian political rules, the country needs to hold an election by October.
sentences.zh: 但根据加拿大的政治规则，国家必须在10月前举行大选。

sentences.en: And so our expectation and Mr. Carney's campaign has indicated this is that he will call for a federal election really early on after his sworn in and seek to capitalize on his momentum to get a mandate at a national level from Canadians.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的预期以及卡尼先生的竞选团队已经表明的是，他将在宣誓就职后不久就宣布举行联邦大选，并试图利用他的势头，从加拿大人那里获得国家层面的授权。

sentences.en: That seems kind of head-spinning.
sentences.zh: 听起来让人头晕目眩。

sentences.en: So he's got to ride the momentum, right?
sentences.zh: 所以他必须顺应这股势头，对吧？

sentences.en: But he also has to be kind of avoiding an all-out trade war with Trump, cut a deal, still look like he's standing up to Trump.
sentences.zh: 但他也必须避免与特朗普爆发全面贸易战，达成协议，同时还要显得自己在对抗特朗普。

sentences.en: This seems like an incredible needle to try to thread.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个极难完成的任务。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: I think it's a really difficult balancing act.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一次非常困难的走钢丝。

sentences.en: In his acceptance speech of the leadership, Mark Carney was barely celebratory, frankly.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，马克·卡尼在党魁胜选演讲中几乎没有什么庆祝的气氛。

sentences.en: The Americans want our resources, our water, our land, our country.
sentences.zh: 美国人想要我们的资源、我们的水、我们的土地、我们的国家。

sentences.en: Think about it.
sentences.zh: 想想看。

sentences.en: If they succeeded, they would destroy our way of life.
sentences.zh: 如果他们成功了，他们就会摧毁我们的生活方式。

sentences.en: He made like a wartime speech and he was clear that he was going to be very aggressive against the United States.
sentences.zh: 他发表了一场类似于战时状态的演讲，并明确表示他将对美国采取非常强硬的立场。

sentences.en: My government will keep our tariffs on until the Americans show us respect.
sentences.zh: 我的政府将继续征收关税，直到美国人表现出对我们的尊重。

sentences.en: That was like a really striking moment.
sentences.zh: 那真是一个极其震撼的时刻。

sentences.en: But at the same time, he's going to have to deal with President Trump.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他将不得不与特朗普总统打交道。

sentences.en: And that kind of rhetoric doesn't play very well with President Trump.
sentences.zh: 而这种言论在特朗普总统那里并吃不开。

sentences.en: So what about Poliev?
sentences.zh: 那么波利耶夫呢？

sentences.en: I can imagine that being a right-wing populist who is compared to Trump is suddenly not a great thing to be in Canada.
sentences.zh: 我可以想象，作为一个被拿来与特朗普作比较的右翼民粹主义者，在加拿大突然不是什么好事。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think that Pierre Poliev is not Trump, but his detractors here in Canada call him Maple MAGA.
sentences.zh: 我认为皮埃尔·波利耶夫不是特朗普，但他在这里的反对者称他为“枫叶MAGA”。

sentences.en: That's kind of the slur they use against him.
sentences.zh: 那是他们用来攻击他的贬义词。

sentences.en: And even though many of his policies are pretty sort of mainstream, vanilla, moderate, conservative policies, he does borrow from the MAGA playbook.
sentences.zh: 尽管他的许多政策相当主流、中庸、温和且保守，但他确实借鉴了MAGA的套路。

sentences.en: And so that is not a great situation to be in when your country suddenly turns against President Trump and everything he stands for in such a huge and visceral way.
sentences.zh: 所以当你的国家突然以如此巨大而强烈的方式反对特朗普总统及其代表的一切时，处境就会变得非常不妙。

sentences.en: Is he trying to put distance between himself and Trump?
sentences.zh: 他是否在试图与特朗普保持距离？

sentences.en: Has he shifted his campaign?
sentences.zh: 他改变竞选策略了吗？

sentences.en: Well, the conservatives are really trying to stage a pivot.
sentences.zh: 嗯，保守党确实在努力谋求转变。

sentences.en: They still have a solid chance at winning the federal election when it happens.
sentences.zh: 在联邦大选到来时，他们仍然有很大的胜算。

sentences.en: According to polls, they're sort of neck and neck with Carney and the liberals.
sentences.zh: 根据民调，他们与卡尼和自由党势均力敌。

sentences.en: But their leader has to just do a whole new thing now.
sentences.zh: 但他们的领袖现在必须采取全新的做法。

sentences.en: So what they're doing is they are really distancing themselves from President Trump,
sentences.zh: 所以他们正在做的是，与特朗普总统真正划清界限，

sentences.en: saying that the rhetoric and the threats coming out of the White House are not what they believe in.
sentences.zh: 声称白宫发出的言论和威胁不是他们的信奉之物。

sentences.en: They're going to stand up to President Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们将挺身对抗特朗普总统。

sentences.en: And recently, President Trump gave an interview to a British magazine and he said, oh, I'm not so sure what I think about this Poliev guy in Canada.
sentences.zh: 最近，特朗普总统接受了一家英国杂志的采访，他说，哦，我不太确定我对加拿大这个波利耶夫有什么看法。

sentences.en: He's not a MAGA guy.
sentences.zh: 他不是个MAGA分子。

sentences.en: And boy, did Pierre Poliev grab that opportunity.
sentences.zh: 天哪，皮埃尔·波利耶夫可真是抓住了这个机会。

sentences.en: The president says that he doesn't like me.
sentences.zh: 总统说他不喜欢我。

sentences.en: He doesn't think that I'm a MAGA guy.
sentences.zh: 他认为我不是个MAGA分子。

sentences.en: I am not.
sentences.zh: 我确实不是。

sentences.en: It is true that I am Canada firSt.
sentences.zh: 承认我是“加拿大优先”是真的。

sentences.en: He says, you're right, Mr. President.
sentences.zh: 他说，您说得对，总统先生。

sentences.en: I'm not a MAGA guy.
sentences.zh: 我不是个MAGA分子。

sentences.en: I'm a Canada first guy.
sentences.zh: 我是个“加拿大优先”的人。

sentences.en: And if that upsets foreign leaders, including the American president, I'm fine with that because I have one job to do is to fight for this country.
sentences.zh: 如果这惹恼了包括美国总统在内的外国领导人，我不在乎，因为我有一项工作要做，那就是为这个国家而战。

sentences.en: We will never be the 51st state.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不会成为第51个州。

sentences.en: And I will always stand up for our flag and our people.
sentences.zh: 我将永远捍卫我们的国旗和我们的人民。

sentences.en: So the opposition party, the conservatives need to sort of reinvent themselves, frankly, more close to the center to have a fighting chance in the elections.
sentences.zh: 因此，反对党保守党坦白说需要进行自我重塑，更贴近政治中心，才能在大选中有一战之力。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of odd moment of political consensus in a country that was five minutes ago going through this incredibly polarizing political situation.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个奇怪的政治共识时刻，就在五分钟前，这个国家还在经历这种极其两极分化的政治局势。

sentences.en: Are either of these candidates articulating what the future of Canada would look like?
sentences.zh: 这两位候选人中有人在阐述加拿大未来的样貌吗？

sentences.en: Are they talking about what would happen if the United States isn't at play anymore?
sentences.zh: 他们在讨论如果美国不再参与其中会发生什么吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely, Kim.
sentences.zh: 当然，金。

sentences.en: And I think that's just been something really interesting to observe.
sentences.zh: 我认为这正是一个非常有趣现象。

sentences.en: There's clearly an existential crisis happening with the Canadian economy.
sentences.zh: 加拿大经济显然正在经历一场生存危机。

sentences.en: And this huge breakdown in the relationship with the United States is driving it home.
sentences.zh: 与美国关系的这种巨大破裂让这一点变得更加痛彻心扉。

sentences.en: So both candidates and both parties are talking a lot about what a future of a successful Canada would look like diversifying away from the United States dependents.
sentences.zh: 因此，两位候选人和两个政党都在大力探讨一个成功的加拿大的未来应该是什么样子，即摆脱对美国的依赖实现多元化。

sentences.en: And part of the reason they want to be doing this urgently is that the situation with the tariffs from the United States is like shifting sands.
sentences.zh: 他们迫切希望这样做的部分原因在于，美国关税政策的情况就像变幻莫测的沙地一样。

sentences.en: The one day it's going to be 25 percent on everything.
sentences.zh: 今天对所有商品征收25%的关税。

sentences.en: The next day that's canceled, but it's going to be 50 percent on steel.
sentences.zh: 第二天取消了，但又要对钢铁征收50%的关税。

sentences.en: And so this is a very destabilizing situation for the Canadian economy.
sentences.zh: 因此，这对加拿大经济来说是一个极度不稳定局势。

sentences.en: And Canada doesn't have a lot of other customers.
sentences.zh: 而且加拿大没有太多其他客户。

sentences.en: They sell most of their stuff to Americans.
sentences.zh: 他们大部分的东西都卖给了美国人。

sentences.en: And that's why they're looking much more toward Europe.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们把目光更多地投向欧洲。

sentences.en: I mean, half of Canadians, according to a recent poll, want to even join the European Union.
sentences.zh: 我是说，根据最近的一项民意调查，一半的加拿大人甚至想加入欧盟。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太惊人了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: That's how far this is going.
sentences.zh: 事情已经发展到这种地步了。

sentences.en: But they're also looking to improve other relationships.
sentences.zh: 但他们也在寻求改善其他关系。

sentences.en: Right now they're in a really tough spot with China, which is another top trading partner.
sentences.zh: 目前他们与另一个顶级贸易伙伴中国正处于非常艰难的境地。

sentences.en: The Chinese have imposed tariffs on Canada, sort of trying to squeeze them not to cut a deal with the United States on tariffs and trade.
sentences.zh: 中方对加拿大征收了关税，试图施压逼迫他们不要在关税和贸易问题上与美国达成交易。

sentences.en: And so they're finding themselves in a really difficult position when they need to strategically rethink their global economic and trade links.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他们需要从战略上重新思考其全球经济和贸易纽带时，他们发现自己陷入了一个非常困难的境地。

sentences.en: And both the liberals and the conservatives are casting a wider net around the world for new best friends.
sentences.zh: 自由党和保守党都在世界各地撒下更广的网，寻找新的好朋友。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Matina, in any good relationship, trust is essential.
sentences.zh: 玛蒂娜，在任何良好的关系中，信任都是必不可少的。

sentences.en: So in this relationship between the United States and Canada, let's say Trump goes back on the tariffs, decides that he wants things back to the way they were with Canada.
sentences.zh: 因此，在美加两国的这种关系中，假设特朗普收回关税决定，决定让一切回到与加拿大以前的状态，

sentences.en: Can the relationship be put back together again?
sentences.zh: 这种关系还能修复吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I think obviously the breach of trust and the uncertainty has already caused a lot of damage, even economically.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为很明显，信任的破裂和不确定性已经造成了巨大的损害，甚至在经济上也是如此。

sentences.en: You know, there's been market volatility, investment has been frozen.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，市场一直在波动，投资已经冻结。

sentences.en: And so folks are already hurting financially here in Canada.
sentences.zh: 因此，这里的加拿大人在经济上已经受到了伤害。

sentences.en: And of course, it goes deeper than that.
sentences.zh: 当然，影响远不止于此。

sentences.en: There's a break in trust that feels really meaningful.
sentences.zh: 这种信任的破裂感觉非常深远。

sentences.en: Right now it does feel kind of permanent, but it is conceivable that in the future there could be perhaps different leaders on both sides and those fences could be mended.
sentences.zh: 目前它确实感觉有点像永久性的，但可以想象的是，未来双方可能会出现不同的领导人，这些裂痕也可以修补。

sentences.en: But it will be on new terMs.
sentences.zh: 但那将建立在新的条款之上。

sentences.en: What I'm seeing here in Canada is a really energized willingness to redefine what it is to be Canadian, both at home and on the world stage,
sentences.zh: 我在加拿大看到的是一种充满活力、热切的意愿，想要重新定义身为加拿大人意味着什么，无论是在国内还是在世界舞台上，

sentences.en: through new economic relationships and more defined cultural references, too.
sentences.zh: 通过建立新的经济关系和更明确的文化认同。

sentences.en: I think even if this episode were to just sort of end tomorrow, it would still have a lasting legacy of seeing a more clear, a more assertive and prouder, a more Canadian Canada.
sentences.zh: 我认为，即使这一事件明天就这么结束了，它仍然会留下深远的影响，让我们看到一个更清晰、更自信、更自豪、更具加拿大特色的加拿大。

sentences.en: Matina, as always, thank you.
sentences.zh: 玛蒂娜，老样子，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，金。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, hours after Trump's global tariffs on steel and aluminum took effect, the Canadian government retaliated with new tariffs on $20 billion of U.S.
sentences.zh: 周三，在特朗普针对钢铁和铝的全球关税生效几小时后，加拿大政府进行了报复，对价值200亿美元的美国商品征收了新关税。

sentences.en: imports.
sentences.zh: 进口商品。

sentences.en: That came as the European Union also hit back with new levies against American goods.
sentences.zh: 此前，欧盟也采取了反击措施，对美国商品征收了新的关税。

sentences.en: Trump, who earlier this week declined to rule out the possibility that his economic policies would cause a recession, vowed to respond, saying, quote,
sentences.zh: 本周早些时候，特朗普拒绝排除其经济政策会导致经济衰退的可能性，他发誓要作出回应，并引述称，

sentences.en: Of course I'll hit back.
sentences.zh: 我当然会反击。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: In what the Trump administration is calling the largest deregulatory announcement in American history,
sentences.zh: 在特朗普政府所称的美国历史上规模最大的放松管制公告中，

sentences.en: the Environmental Protection Agency Wednesday said it would unwind dozens of regulations, among them protections for wetlands and limits on how much soot can pour from smokestacks.
sentences.zh: 环境保护署周三表示，将取消数十项规定，其中包括对湿地的保护以及对烟囱排放烟尘量的限制。

sentences.en: Most significantly,
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，

sentences.en: the administration plans to erase the EPA's legal authority to regulate greenhouse gases by reconsidering decades of science that highlight the dangers of global warming.
sentences.zh: 通过重新审视几十年来强调全球变暖危险的科学研究，该政府计划消除环保署监管温室气体的法定权力。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Shannon Lynn, Nina Feldman, Michael Simon-Johnson, and Anna Foley, with help from Alex Stern and Stella Tan.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由香农·林恩、妮娜·费尔德曼、迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊和安娜·福利制作，亚历克斯·斯特恩和斯特拉·陈提供了协助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Chris Haxel, Devin Taylor, and M.J.
sentences.zh: 节目由克里斯·哈克塞尔、德文·泰勒和M.J.

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn, contains original music by Dan Powell and Sophia Landman, and was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩剪辑，包含丹·鲍威尔和索菲亚·兰德曼的原创音乐，由阿莉莎·莫克斯利工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brumberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由来自Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Severson.
sentences.zh: 我是金·西弗森。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党陷入了一场激烈、混乱、有时甚至令人惊心动魄的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我莎拉·凯尼格主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，我们将讲述人们试图维持其影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 都市。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
